solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tree where duck engaged by some trill?

indicators.note: to be engaged by something is to be held within it, so the duck sits inside the trill

parts.note: a trill alternates two notes rapidly, ba-ba-ba-ba, and a stretch of it gives BABAB
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, written as the round letter O

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher asks which tree a warbling bird is singing from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' just joins definition and wordplay. The trill is written out as the sound it makes, two alternating notes, and only part of it is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is an African tree with a famously swollen trunk, a plain example of the defining word.

clue.text: Tree remains after forest fire?

definitions.meaning: the common European hardwood of the olive family, Fraxinus
the powdery residue left once wood has burnt

explanation.surface: Wondering which tree survives after a blaze sweeps the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a familiar hardwood and the grey powder left once anything has burnt away.

clue.text: Entrance of beautiful girl in play for the nation

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening letter, so only the start of beautiful is used

parts.note: Olivia is the countess in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night

explanation.surface: A lovely young actress makes her stage entrance in a play staged for the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads as a stage entry but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a landlocked South American country, so it is one example of a nation.

clue.text: Magoo's good-natured game

parts.note: Mr Magoo, the cartoon character, was so short-sighted he was practically blind, so Magoo's means belonging to a sightless man
bluff can mean hearty and frank in a genial way

explanation.surface: Describes a cartoon character's cheerful way of playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Magoo was really very short-sighted, not blind, so the clue takes a little licence. The game is also known as blind man's buff.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's party pastime in which a blindfolded player gropes around to catch the others.

clue.text: You've been caught cold in superhero's city, dropping back

indicators.note: the cold letter is placed inside the shortened city name
the back of the city name, its last letter, is dropped

parts.note: Gotham City is Batman's home town
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone catches a chill in Batman's city and their back gives out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping back' shortens GOTHAM to GOTHA before C goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang exclamation said on catching someone out, equivalent to telling them they've been nabbed.

clue.text: Order restraining granny is for seedy practice

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the order letters go round the others

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
nan is an informal word for a grandmother
taken as written

explanation.surface: A court order keeping grandma away because of what she does is sordid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seedy' is a pun: the practice wastes seed, as in Onan's story in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means masturbation or withdrawal, named after Onan, who spilled his seed, hence the punning seedy.

clue.text: Big firm belly

definitions.meaning: a large company or incorporated business
a humorous old word for a large paunch

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a muscular, solid stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a large incorporated company and, jokingly, a sizeable pot-belly.

clue.text: Extremes of language? Weep three times, 'cos terribly upset on holiday

parts.note: the letters at either end of the alphabet, the building blocks of written language, are A and Z

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: T is short for time, and three of them are needed
the informal shortening of because, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone on holiday cries and cries because of how badly things are going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremes of language' points to A and Z, the alphabet's ends. 'terribly' mixes WEEP, TTT and COS into TECTWOSTEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for traveller's diarrhoea caught in Mexico, like Montezuma's revenge: a stomach complaint abroad.

clue.text: Formal introduction suggested error said before a maiden

indicators.note: this word only joins the neighbouring pieces: it says which one stands next to which in the answer

parts.note: read as 'error said' made mad, with the anagram signal mad only suggested: the jumbled letters of error said followed by that implied word itself
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A formal speech opener is put forward, though an error is spoken before a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is never printed: 'suggested' says it is implied, and that implied word, mad, is then itself written into the answer ahead of the article and the maiden. Rearranging ERROR SAID gives DEARSIROR.
explanation.definitionFit: The conventional salutation opening a business letter to an unnamed recipient.

clue.text: Burner, cold one

parts.note: a chill is a coldness
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something that burns, yet cold: a contradictory pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burner' sounds like a stove but means something that burns the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot pepper scorches the tongue, so it is fairly called a burner.

clue.text: Old sovereign, a particular age

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for a queen, here a past one

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch belongs to a certain historical period.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a distinct period of history, such as the Victorian one.

clue.text: Groovy thing to have sex!

definitions.meaning: a groove or furrow, as worn by wheels
to be in the mating season, as stags are

explanation.surface: Sounds like a swinging-sixties invitation to get intimate.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names a worn track and also the mating activity of deer and similar animals.

clue.text: One elasticated item — or four?

definitions.meaning: a single set of stretchy straps holding up trousers, called suspenders in the US
a brace is two, so two lots of two make four

explanation.surface: A query whether an item of elastic clothing counts as one thing or four.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouser straps are sold as a single set, while a brace means a couple, so two of them total four.

clue.text: So long fluffy rice came first?

indicators.note: first puts the word for came at the front of the charade

parts.note: arrived means came

indicators.note: fluffy rice has its grains loosened, so these letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Leaving a long time to cook the rice, perhaps hoping it comes out fluffy.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian farewell, equivalent to goodbye or see you later.

clue.text: Pound in US dollars as concealed figure

indicators.note: to pound is to beat or batter, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Pound sterling expressed in US dollars, exchange rates as a hidden number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the currency beside dollars; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Each wooden doll nests inside a bigger one, so every figure but the outer one is kept out of sight.

clue.text: Giant, light having shed skin

indicators.note: losing its skin means the word loses its outermost letters at both ends

parts.note: a torch is a portable light

explanation.surface: A huge creature, like a lamp, that has moulted.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcs are monstrous beings of fantasy fiction, and the word also once meant an ogre or sea monster.

clue.text: God gaining ultimate of respect in trip across Africa as emperor

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god

indicators.note: the final letter sits inside the trip

parts.note: a safari is an expedition, especially in Africa

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter of respect is used

explanation.surface: A deity earns respect on an African journey, hailed as an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Ras Tafari was the title and name of Haile Selassie before he became Emperor of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: The name Haile Selassie bore before being crowned Ethiopia's ruler, revered as divine by Rastafarians.

clue.text: Beastly remark from far right escaping US actress

indicators.note: the far right letters get away, leaving the rest of the name

parts.note: Mia Farrow, star of Rosemary's Baby
far taken as written plus R for right

explanation.surface: A political extremist says something nasty after getting away from an American film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far right' looks political; it is FAR plus R, removed from MIAFARROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's call is the remark of an animal, hence the punning beastly.

clue.text: Pass off as fake ring held by hand

indicators.note: the ring is held within the hand, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A con artist palms a fake ring, holding it in his hand to fool a buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose something unwanted or spurious on someone deceitfully, as in palming off a counterfeit.

clue.text: God taking ecstasy for an interval

parts.note: Triton is a Greek sea god, son of Poseidon
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A deity takes a drug during a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interval' suggests a break, but it is the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the span of three whole tones, the augmented fourth once called the devil's interval.

clue.text: They're thick, some this stupid banking zilch

indicators.note: to bank is to keep something safely, so the shuffled letters hold the nothing within them
stupid suggests muddled thinking, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: zilch means nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: Some dim people are this stupid about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thick' reads as stupid but means dense in texture. 'stupid' jumbles SOME THIS to SMOTHIES, which holds O.
explanation.definitionFit: Blended fruit drinks are dense in texture, so these drinks fairly describe themselves as thick.

clue.text: Metal wrapper up to wrapping up dope

indicators.note: the word for up to is wrapped round the information

parts.note: til is a short form of until, up to
dope is slang for information

explanation.surface: A metallic package that's going to hide drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs but means information.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheeting used to wrap food, so it is literally a metallic wrapping.

clue.text: Race to publish

definitions.meaning: to race is to go at speed, sprint
to ... a story in a newspaper is to print it

explanation.surface: An editor hurrying to get a story into print.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both sprinting and a newspaper printing a story.

clue.text: Intensity of light in Milan needing clue that's cryptic

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscure and puzzling, so these letters are hidden in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in Milan struggles to brighten a puzzling clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The physics term for how much light falls on a surface, measured in lux.

clue.text: Avian sound in place of chickens? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite the full word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a coop is an enclosure for poultry

explanation.surface: A bird noise heard in a hen house, though not exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft murmuring call of a dove or pigeon, a bird noise.

clue.text: Some bozo, a fool?

indicators.note: only some of the letters in these words are needed, a run tucked inside them

explanation.surface: Asks whether some clown is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as giving it: bozo and fool both describe it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy, stupid person is the same as a bozo or a fool.

clue.text: Thingamy having back-to-back parties — that's cute!

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: back to back means the second party faces the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a second do, another party
ah is the fond exclamation at something sweet

explanation.surface: A gadget from successive parties wins an admiring sigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-back' sounds like one after the other, but here the two parties face away from each other, so the second is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A vague word for an item whose name escapes you, like whatsit.

clue.text: Closely follow gorilla

explanation.surface: Tailing a big primate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for copying someone and a noun for a large primate.

clue.text: Second change

definitions.meaning: the medal for coming second place

explanation.surface: Seems to be about a moment's alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: One metal names the runner-up's medal and the small coins of loose cash.

clue.text: Style for swimmer

definitions.meaning: a haircut short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: Seems to praise a swimmer's form in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names an infamous hairdo and a common food fish.
